items.title: Harold Dejan Interview, 1979-12-07
items.q: Like Henry Glass was calling Booker T and Sun Fu Klo, which is a little to Eureka. And had some pretty good bass drummers

ctx.x: I believe some time ago you said that the, you know, from what I read in the jazz archives, the interview in jazz archives, you said that the parade music had actually gotten worse.

And you attributed it to the, I suppose, the bass drum, the drummers aren't as good. Well, no, no, they're not as good as the drummers used to be. Oh. I got a drummer, his daddy was, oh, his daddy was a, was a drummer, Brooker T. Henry Glass, get him. And, uh, so he, uh, the reason, I guess the reason why he played like he played, not because he was following behind his dad since he was a little bitty thing, you know, holding on his daddy's coat tail while his daddy was playing the bass drums. And, uh, that's…
You know, when you were talking to me over the phone you said sometimes you play three funerals in one day.
